words.definition: A state of serious or continued difficulty and misfortune.
to shock or excite someone into taking action
to waste something valuable (money, time, an opportunity) carelessly
to confirm or support a claim with additional evidence
to make an unpleasant feeling (fear, guilt, grief) less intense
to come together and form one whole (of ideas, groups, forces)
to speak about someone or something as if it has little worth
to deliberately avoid or abstain from something
to calm someone's anger, usually by concessions or soothing words
to struggle clumsily; to be in serious difficulty without making progress
to explain or dwell on a point far longer than necessary
honest, open, and sincere expression; frankness
a confusing and difficult problem with no easy answer
seriousness and dignity of manner that commands respect
a deadlock; a situation where no progress or agreement is possible
a supposed cure-all; a single solution for all problems (often used skeptically)
an unexpected piece of good fortune, especially a sudden gain of money
the person or thing holding a whole arrangement together; the essential element
sharpness of judgment and quick insight, especially in business or practical matters
a complicated, entangling situation that is hard to escape (literally: a bog)
the defining spirit or mood of a particular period in history
sharp at accurately assessing situations and turning them to advantage
done as a routine duty, with minimal effort or care
very weak, thin, or slight; barely holding (of a connection, argument, grip)
present or found everywhere at once
harshly and wittily critical (of a remark, review, report)
friendly, warm, and easy to talk to
having sharp practical judgment, often with a hint of cunning
excessively intricate and hard to follow (of arguments, plots, processes)
refusing absolutely to change one's mind or position
skillful and quick, whether with the hands or in handling situations
to strengthen or support something so it holds up better
to make something bad less severe or harmful
to reduce, restrict, or cut something short
to describe or mark out precisely where something begins and ends
to extend known facts into an estimate about the unknown
to emphasize; to show why something matters
to establish something so firmly it becomes hard to change
a warning or condition attached to a statement or agreement
an earlier case or decision used as a guide for later ones
a division into two sharply contrasting things
a natural tendency to behave in a particular way
understanding of an event only after it has happened
a hidden danger or easy-to-make mistake
a standard point of reference for comparing or judging
most noticeable or most important; standing out
dealing with things practically rather than idealistically
extremely careful and precise about details
showing careful, sensible judgment about the future
expressed briefly and clearly
hard to find, catch, or pin down
